REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 8, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 869 8871 9290
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS AND THE PUBLIC MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public subject to Los Angeles County mandated COVID-19 protocols. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will also be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below, or in-person subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using any of the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86988719290
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 869 8871 9290
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD
THURSDAY, APRIL 8, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED
BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 869 8871 9290

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A Proclamation was made by the City Council as follows:

  Dionisia Paulo Gamboa (in honor of her 100th birthday celebration on April 8, 2021).

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer provided an update on the City’s public meeting schedule.

5B.  Closed Session reports from the Friday, April 2, 2021, 1:00 p.m. and Tuesday, April 6,
  2021, 10:00 a.m. City Council Special Meetings

  Pam Lee, Interim City Attorney, provided the following reports:

  The City Council met in Closed Session to discuss Item 5A as listed on the Friday, April 2,
  2021, 1:00 p.m. City Council Special Meeting Agenda:

  5A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  With regard to Item 5A, the City Council discussed the matter and no reportable action
  was taken.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 8

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  The City Council met in Closed Session to discuss Item 5A as listed on the Tuesday, April
  6, 2021, 10:00 a.m. City Council Special Meeting Agenda:

  5A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  With regard to Item 5A, the City Council discussed the matter and no reportable action
  was taken.

  This concluded the Closed Session reports.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Alejandro Estella spoke regarding concern with the City’s mileage reimbursement and auto
  allowance programs and requested a written response to his inquiries.

  Leopoldo Lopez spoke regarding concern that his claim against the City has not be
  reconciled in a timely fashion and requested an update on the claim’s status.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding his support for a potential mural to be included in the City’s Art
  in Public Places Program.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding the difference between elected versus appointed City
  Councilmembers, the definition of public places under the City’s Art in Public Places
  program as stated in the Cerritos Municipal Code and requested clarification regarding art
  pieces located indoors, his concern there were no evening meeting or weekend times
  scheduled for the City Charter review, and requested clarification regarding the appointed
  City Treasurer position.

  Murali Vasudevan expressed concern regarding the allowable locations for art pieces funded
  by the City’s Art in Public Places program, pending items to be brought before the various
  City Commissions, and the City’s pine tree removal program.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, March 22, 2021, 2:00 p.m. City Council Special Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Monday, March
  22, 2021, 2:00 p.m. City Council Special Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  Thursday, March 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Thursday, March
  25, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated April 8, 2021 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of Demands
  as follows:

  City of Cerritos  April 8, 2021  $ 3,609,864.78 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports

  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending February 28,
  2021 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending February 28, 2021
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 8

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the COVID-
  19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum provided general remarks.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to receive and file the
  informational report on the City's response to the COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of a request for City Council direction regarding the potential
  revision and expansion of existing Cerritos Municipal Code regulations pertaining to drive-
  through service restaurants (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Michael DiGangi spoke in support of proposed changes to the Cerritos Municipal Code
  regulations pertaining to drive-through service restaurants.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding the potential long-term negative impacts as related to any
  changes to the Cerritos Municipal Code regulations pertaining to drive-through service
  restaurants and which criteria the City will use to select restaurants who request such land-
  use.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Direct staff to prepare an analysis pertaining to drive-through service restaurants,
  utilizing the City’s conservative approach to such land-use matters, inclusive of a
  financial and sales tax revenue evaluation and with consideration of protecting the City
  of Cerritos’ aesthetic image and quality of life; and

  2. Prepare an agenda report with the analysis findings, inclusive of any proposed
  development code amendments necessary to formally amend existing regulations and a
  CEQA environmental analysis for any such amendments and related entitlements for
  review and consideration by the Cerritos Planning Commission and City Council at
  future publicly noticed meetings (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of a negotiated settlement agreement in the case City of Signal
  Hill, et al. v. Central Basin Municipal Water District regarding fixed meter charges
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water & Power.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Leticia Vasquez-Wilson submitted written correspondence regarding imposing meter
  charges on water customers and suggested more involvement in an effort to reduce the
  likelihood of unnecessary litigation in the future.

  Noting there were no others individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Approve the settlement agreement and mutual release by and between Central Basin
  Municipal Water District, the Board of Directors of Central Basin Municipal Water
  District, and those water purveyor Members of the Central Basin Municipal Water
  District who are Petitioners in Los Angeles County Superior Court Case Number
  19STCP03882 titled City of Signal Hill v. Central Basin Municipal Water District being
  Cities of Signal Hill, Lakewood, Paramount, Downey, Vernon, Santa Fe Springs, Tract
  349 Mutual Water Company, Montebello Land and Water Company, Maywood Mutual
  Water Company No. 3, Bellflower-Somerset Mutual Water Company, South Montebello
  Irrigation District, Pico Water District, City of Cerritos, La Habra Heights County Water
  District, Cities of Pico Rivera, Norwalk, South Gate, Walnut Park Mutual Water
  Company, Tract 180 Water Company, Orchard Dale Water District, Cities of Commerce,
  and Huntington Park City of Signal Hill, et al. v. Central Basin Municipal Water District;
  and

  2. Authorize the Mayor to execute the settlement agreement and mutual release in a form
  approved by the City Attorney (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS TO REINSTATE THE CITY AS A MEMBER OF THE
  ORANGELINE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DBA ECO-RAPID TRANSIT (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Torrey Contreras, Senior Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed. Michael Kodama, Orangeline Development Authority/Eco-Rapid
  Transit representative, was present to respond to City Council inquiries regarding this
  matter.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke in opposition to the West Santa Ana Branch Line Project.

  Michael Kodama, Orangeline Development Authority/Eco-Rapid Transit representative,
  spoke noting the organization’s support for the City of Cerritos rejoining as a member.

  Mel Cortez spoke expressing support for the City rejoining the subject organization, and
  encourage the City as a member to exert influence with regard to the negative impacts of
  the West Santa Ana Branch Line Project on the community.

  Jay Gray inquired as to the City’s motive for rejoining the subject organization and
  requested the City’s appointed representative not support any proposed “mag-lev” efforts
  and donate any stipends for attendance at the organization’s meetings to the City’s General
  Fund.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2021-05, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS TO REINSTATE THE CITY AS A
  MEMBER OF THE ORANGELINE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DBA ECO-RAPID
  TRANSIT, inclusive of the appropriation of approximately $17,000 of restricted
  Proposition A and/or Proposition C funding for OLDA/Eco-Rapid Transit annual
  membership dues (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Designate Councilmember Barrows to serve as the City’s OLDA/Eco-Rapid Transit
  representative (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 8

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  None.

12.  Closed Session

  Pam Lee, Interim City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session
  to discuss the items listed on the Closed Session agenda. An announcement regarding any
  reportable action resulting from the Closed Session will be made at the next regular
  meeting.

  12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE APPOINTMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT: The City Council reconvened to Open Session. Vida
  Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer reported the City Council recessed to Closed Session to
  discuss Items 12A and 12B on the Closed Session agenda. With regard to Item 12A, the
  City Council discussed the matter and there was no further action to report. With regard
  to Item 12B, the City Council took the following action:

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Select Bill Ihrke and the firm of Rutan & Tucker to serve as the Cerritos City Attorney,
  subject to negotiation of a contract for legal services and the terms and conditions
  related thereto. In compliance with the California Brown Act, an item will be placed on
  the Thursday, April 22, 2021, 7:00 p.m. Council/Agency Regular Meeting agenda for
  review and consideration of the contract, inclusive of final terms and conditions; and

  2. Retain the services of Interim City Attorney Pam Lee and the firm of Aleshire & Wynder
  LLC, for a period of six (6) months to complete assigned projects (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Barrows, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Councilmember Yokoyama stated that there was a motion made by himself, and seconded
  by Mayor Pro Tem Vo, to select Pam Lee to serve as the Cerritos City Attorney. He reported
  the motion did not pass pursuant to a 2 – 3 vote.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 8 of 8

12.  Closed Session (continued)

  Councilmember Barrows stated that the motion reported by Councilmember Yokoyama was
  a substitute motion to the main motion, and confirmed the substitute motion failed
  pursuant to a 2 – 3 vote.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 10:55 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
